author: golden state today
title: Qatar Airways announces new ultra-long routes amid ongoing fleet challenges
text:
Qatar Airways, the world’s 11th-largest airline for international flights, announced on June 2 that it will launch or resume ten ultra-long-haul routes between June 2026 and March 2027. The carrier, which operates a fleet of 241 passenger aircraft without a domestic market, ranks fourth globally for long-haul services.
The ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran has significantly affected Qatar Airways’ operations. The airline has suspended flights to more than 22 cities and parked approximately 20% of its fleet as of late May. Its Airbus A380 subfleet remains grounded but is scheduled to return to service in mid-June.
Among the upcoming changes is Qatar Airways’ new longest passenger service: starting July 22, a twice-weekly flight from Doha Hamad International Airport to Bogotá via Caracas using a Boeing 777-200LR. The route will later reverse direction from Doha to Caracas via Bogotá to address operational challenges related to Bogotá’s high elevation. This one-stop link is timed at up to 20 hours and 50 minutes.
Other notable long-haul routes include Auckland back to Doha via Adelaide (up to 20 hours and 30 minutes), Canberra back to Doha via Melbourne (17 hours and 55 minutes), nonstop Doha-Los Angeles (17 hours and 50 minutes), and Doha-San Francisco (17 hours and 30 minutes). These operations are subject to change depending on scheduling adjustments through March next year.
Flights such as those connecting Miami International Airport benefit from Qatar Airways’ partnership with American Airlines within the oneworld alliance. Between April 2025 and March 2026, booking data shows that around 90,000 passengers traveled through Miami en route between other global destinations using Qatar Airways connections.
